## Geometry, emergence, and quantum consistency {.hero-title}

:::: {.hero-lead}
I use asymptotic Hodge theory and Calabi–Yau geometry to understand boundary
regimes of string compactifications—where towers of states become light, strings
emerge, and effective theories encounter quantum-consistency constraints.

:::::: {.home-section .research-focus}

::::: {.section-heading-centered}
## Research focus

I study how geometry controls the microscopic physics of string compactifications,
with emphasis on asymptotic regimes and quantum consistency.
:::::

::::: {.theme-grid}

:::: {.theme-card}
![](assets/icon-emergence.svg){.theme-icon}

### Emergent strings and infinite distance

Identifying the strings, towers of states, and higher-dimensional descriptions that
emerge at boundaries of moduli space.
::::

:::: {.theme-card}
![](assets/icon-hodge.svg){.theme-icon}

### Asymptotic Hodge theory

Turning structural theorems for degenerating Hodge structures into tools for periods,
metrics, couplings, and flux potentials.
::::

:::: {.theme-card}
![](assets/icon-obstruction.svg){.theme-icon}

### Quantum consistency and finiteness

Testing when classical limits survive quantum corrections and how geometry constrains
the landscape of effective theories and flux vacua.
::::

:::::
::::::

Physical Review D 113 (2026)
:::

### Quantum obstructions for $\mathcal{N}=1$ infinite-distance limits — Part II: Kähler obstructions

Quantum corrections in the Kähler sector can enforce correlated scalings among
moduli, obstructing classical infinite-distance limits.

::: {.work-links}
[↗ arXiv:2603.13470](https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.13470)
[◉ DOI](https://doi.org/10.1103/ypyx-mg6r)
:::

JHEP 03 (2026) 063
:::

### Physics and geometry of complex-structure limits in Type IIB Calabi–Yau compactifications

A geometric interpretation of type II, III, and IV limits and the towers of BPS states
that realise their emergent higher-dimensional physics.

::: {.work-links}
[↗ arXiv:2509.07056](https://arxiv.org/abs/2509.07056)
